title: Navigating AI for Testing: Insights on Context and Evaluation with Sourcegraph
description:
In this episode, Simon Maple dives into the world of AI testing with Rishabh Mehrotra from Sourcegraph. Together, they explore the essential aspects of AI in development, focusing on how models need context to create effective tests, the importance of evaluation, and the implications of AI-generated code. Rishabh shares his expertise on when and how AI tests should be conducted, balancing latency and quality, and the critical role of unit tests. They also discuss the evolving landscape of machine learning, the challenges of integrating AI into development workflows, and practical strategies for developers to leverage AI tools like Cody for improved productivity. Whether you're a seasoned developer or just beginning to explore AI in coding, this episode is packed with insights and best practices to elevate your development process.

Chapters
00:15 Introduction - Simon Maple introduces the topic of AI testing and the guest, Rishabh Mehrotra from Sourcegraph.
01:43 The Big Code Problem - Rishabh discusses the challenges of managing large code bases in enterprises and introduces Cody.
04:09 Evolution of AI and ML in Coding - Rishabh shares his journey in AI and the rapid evolution of AI models.
07:11 Features of Cody - An in-depth look at Cody's functionalities, including code completion, code editing, and unit test generation.
13:13 Importance of Evaluation - Rishabh emphasizes the critical role of evaluation metrics in machine learning.
16:36 Custom Commands and Open Context - Discussion on how custom commands and Open Context enhance Cody's flexibility and accuracy.
20:35 The Future of AI in Development - Insights into the future integration of AI tools in development workflows and the need for human oversight.
26:22 Human-in-the-Loop - The importance of human oversight in guiding AI systems to meet desired outcomes.
30:22 Summary and Takeaways - Key takeaways from the episode, emphasizing the importance of evaluation, custom commands, and human oversight.
